title: The Audit Decides the Verdict: Instrument Effects Rival Demographic Bias in LLM Decision Audits
abstract: arXiv:2609.09048v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Whether a language model looks demographically biased can depend on how the audit asks its question. A charitable-aid benchmark reports that the same models favor minority applicants when rating requests one at a time and penalize some when ranking side by side. We test whether that reversal generalizes to hiring, lending, and medical triage: 40,726 requests to five models, applications differing only in the applicant's name, and a primary test fixed before collection. It does not. None of 36 planned contrasts survives correction. The rating advantage keeps its sign at roughly half the published size, and a precision extension bounds any hiring ranking penalty below the published effect, though the lending and triage ranking floors sit above that margin, so the exclusion is conclusive for hiring ranking and for rating in all three domains only. translated_title: 审计决定结论：在LLM决策审计中，工具效应与人口统计学偏差相抗衡
translated_abstract: 语言模型是否看起来存在人口统计学偏差，可能取决于审计如何提出问题。一项慈善援助基准研究报告称，同样的模型在逐个评分请求时偏向少数族裔申请人，而在并排排名时则对部分申请人不利。我们测试了这种反转是否适用于招聘、贷款和医疗分诊领域：向五个模型发送了40,726次请求，申请材料仅在申请人姓名上有所不同，且主要检验在数据收集之前就已预先确定。结果显示这种反转并不存在。36个预先计划的对比中没有一个在校正后依然显著。评分优势保持原有的符号方向，但规模约为已发表结果的一半；一项精度扩展分析将招聘排名惩罚的上限约束在低于已发表效应的水平，不过贷款和分诊排名的置信下限高于该边界，因此排除性结论仅对招聘排名以及全部三个领域的评分任务具有决定性。植入的偏差能追踪其注入的大小，并对原始基准进行了方向性复现……（原文在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文通过涉及五个模型、40,726次请求、覆盖招聘、贷款和医疗分诊的预注册大规模审计发现，先前文献报告的LLM在评分与排名任务中表现相反的人口偏差反转并不能推广，证明审计工具（提问方式）本身的影响与人口统计学偏差同样重要。
en_tdlr: A pre-registered audit of 40,726 requests to five models across hiring, lending, and medical triage shows that the previously reported reversal between LLM rating and ranking demographic biases fails to generalize, demonstrating that audit instrument effects rival demographic bias itself.
